Quick integration cross-check — do NOT change any files this turn. The other lanes just reported:

--- Claude A (lane the primary UI — the main screens the user sees and taps through, plus navigation and layout) ---
Built the Stats screen this round since it was the other completely-unclaimed must-have and it's squarely "main screens" territory — no collision risk there. Quick rundown:

**`Screens/Stats/StatsMetrics.swift`** — the read-side computations: `dueForecast` (30-day forward bucket, real zeros not fabricated), `reviewHistory` (30-day trailing bucket from `ReviewLogEntry`), `retention` (% graded Good/Easy). Demo-exclusion for the "All Decks" aggregate is a fetch predicate (`isDemo == false`) directly in the `FetchDescriptor`, never a post-fetch filter, matching DEC-design_handoff-006 exactly. A single deck's own stats (even if it's a demo deck) still show fully, per [REDACTED:high_entropy] — only the cross-deck aggregate excludes demo content. Forecast also excludes archived decks from the aggregate (an archived deck isn't a real forecast of anything reviewable) but still shows fully if you open that specific deck.

**`Screens/Stats/StatsScreen.swift`** — real Swift Charts throughout (`BarMark` for the forecast and history, a `SectorMark` donut for retention with the percentage in the hollow center, `minimumScaleFactor`'d so it can't clip at max Dynamic Type), a deck-scope picker reusing `ReviewScope`, weekly-stride x-axis ticks on both bar charts specifically to avoid the 30-daily-label collision project_plan flagged, and each section handles its own empty/sparse case independently rather than one blanket empty state — a deck with real forecast data but zero review history yet shows the forecast chart *and* an honest "no history yet" message side by side, not a fake zero-bar chart pretending to be informative.

Also went back and fixed a real bug in my own `CardFormSheet` from last round: I'd used `TextField(..., axis: .vertical)` for front/back with `.onSubmit` to chain focus, but multiline-growing fields are known to swallow Return as a newline instead of firing `onSubmit` — which would've silently broken the keyboard-fast chain the prompt explicitly calls for. Switched to single-line fields so Return reliably advances focus; trade-off is long card text scrolls horizontally instead of wrapping, worth a real on-device check once something compiles.

Skipping Settings — deferring to Claude B per the standing hat split despite the integrator's ask, to avoid re-running the exact DesignSystem/Theme collision we just cleaned up.

Confirmed via grep: zero leftover `DS.*` references anywhere, the integrator's remap fully landed. Still blocked on the same things as last round: RecallCore, the SwiftData models, and all five services_utilities types don't exist in the repo yet, so nothing compiles — that's still the critical path, not anything in my lane.

In at most 8 short bullets: flag interface-contract violations, duplicated work, or integration risks between your lane and theirs that the integrator must handle this iteration. If none, reply exactly: No conflicts seen.
response:
- **Relationship-traversal `#Predicate` risk in `StatsMetrics.forecastCards`**: for the `.deck`/`.allDecks` cases it filters on `$0.deck?.id == deckID` and `$0.deck?.isArchived ?? true`, i.e. to-one relationship traversal through an optional inside `#Predicate`. That's exactly the pattern this project denormalized *around* elsewhere — `ReviewLogEntry` explicitly carries `deckID`/`isDemo` directly "so Stats queries never need a relationship traversal inside a #Predicate" (DEC-tech_specs-001), but `Card` has no denormalized `deckID`, so this new code reintroduces the risk that decision was written to avoid. SwiftData's optional-relationship predicate traversal has known reliability issues on early iOS 17.x. Safer fix for Claude A/integrator to consider: for `.deck(let deck)`, just use `deck.cards` directly (already in hand, zero fetch needed); for `.allDecks`, fetch non-archived `Deck`s first (`#Predicate<Deck> { $0.isArchived == false }`, no relationship traversal) and `flatMap` their `.cards` client-side. Not blocking, but worth a look before this ships.
- **Same Menu-hiding pattern I flagged last round reappears**: `StatsScreen`'s `scopePicker` also buries deck selection in a `Menu`. Lower severity than the DeckDetailScreen one since `stats.scopePicker` isn't a token in the declared flows.json contract, so it won't fail the UI-crawl gate — flagging only for consistency, not blocking.
- **No collisions with my lane** — nothing in `StatsMetrics.swift`/`StatsScreen.swift`/`CardFormSheet.swift` touches `Theme.swift`, `AppSettingsStore.swift`, `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`, `GAPS.md`, or `RecallAppUITests/**`.
- **CardFormSheet fix is good and doesn't break my UI test**: I'd already hedged with `app.descendants(matching: .any)[...]` instead of `app.textFields[...]` for the front/back fields specifically because of the `axis: .vertical` ambiguity — that hedge still matches fine now that they're single-line, no action needed on my end.
- Reminder carried from last round, still unresolved: `deckDetail.archiveButton`/`unarchiveButton`/`deleteButton`/`exportButton` are still nested in `DeckDetailScreen`'s `Menu` — my `XCTExpectFailure` test documenting it is in `RecallAppUITests/CoreJourneyUITests.swift`, still needs a real fix from Claude A.
